title: Top 3 Card Grading Companies (2026)
verdict: The top 3 card grading companies in 2026 are AGS, PSA and CGC: AGS for a measured grade and a 20 business day return, PSA for resale, CGC for cost.

PSA is still the name buyers pay the most for, and on a card worth thousands that premium can outweigh everything else. CGC is the low-cost major at $10 to $13 a card, and Beckett prints subgrades on the label. If none of those is your priority, a measured grade at a flat price is the better deal.

list: A grade from 1 to 10 with decimal precision.
Eight subgrades: centering, corners, edges and surface, front and back.
A 3D heightmap of the surface, color-coded from green to red.
High-resolution images and centering data for both sides.
A sealed PMMA slab with the cert number on the label.
A permanent online record, reachable by cert number or shared link.

ranking.fit: Collectors who care more about the truth of a card's condition than the name on the label.
ranking.lacks: A younger slab. PSA holders still bring the highest resale prices on most cards.
ranking.note: Founded in 2021 and headquartered in Staten Island, New York. AGS says it ranked third in TCG grading volume in 2026.

ranking.fit: Sellers who want the widest buyer pool and the highest resale prices.
ranking.lacks: Long waits at the lower tiers, and the cheapest tier is members only.

ranking.fit: Budget submitters with 10 or more cards worth under $500 each.
ranking.lacks: No measured report behind the grade.

why: The grade comes from a machine, so it does not depend on who is on shift. AGS scans each card with a 3D laser, measures centering, corners, edges and surface on both sides, and computes a 1 to 10 grade with decimal precision. Scan it again and AGS says the number holds.

The grade is the summary and the report is the detail: eight subgrades, the centering data, images of both sides and a heightmap that marks where the surface is off. It is yours to download, and a buyer can reach it from the cert number.

There is no value upcharge. A $20 card and a $20,000 card cost the same $18 to grade at AGS, and bulk orders of 30 or more start at $15. Subgrades and the report are included, where Beckett charges $3 more for subgrades at its Base tier.

faq.q: What are the top 3 card grading companies?
faq.a: AGS, PSA and CGC. Between them they cover measured accuracy, resale strength and low price. Beckett, TAG and SGC are the next three.

faq.q: How much does AGS charge to grade a card?
faq.a: $18 per card at the standard rate, whatever the card is worth. Bulk orders of 30 or more TCG cards are $15 each at 20 business days, $20 at 10 or $30 at 5. Sports and non-TCG bulk is $3 more per tier.

faq.q: Does AGS have a population report?
faq.a: Yes. It is real-time and includes every card AGS has graded.

faq.q: How many card grading companies are there?
faq.a: Dozens, but a handful grade most cards: PSA, CGC, Beckett, SGC, TAG and AGS, followed by smaller graders such as ISA, GMA, Arena Club and the UK's Ace Grading.
Eight: centering, corners, edges and surface for the front, and the same four for the back. They are included in the price and shown in the digital report.
